title: CI: parallelize the recycled-bit frame-pair checks (~2x on the critical path)
body:
**CI speedup only.** No mathematical change and no new κ.

## Why

`verify-recycled-bit` is the critical path of the `verify` workflow. On a recent run of #210 it took 1,009 s (3.11), 842 s (3.14) and 725 s (3.13), while every other group finished in under 10 minutes. Profiling `research/recycled-bit-integration/verify.py --all` shows setup takes 3 s and almost all the remaining time is two single-threaded loops:

- 4,878 new frame pairs: nesting and nondegeneracy (about 176 s serial);
- every distinct inherited ledger move: nesting (about 9 minutes serial).

## Change

Each check is a pure function of the shared `Exact` frames. `check_moves` splits the moves across forked worker processes and returns every move that fails; the verifier asserts that list is empty.

- The checks are the same `exact.inside` and `exact.nondegenerate` calls as before. Only which process evaluates them changes.
- Moves are grouped by target key, so each worker builds each annihilator basis once.
- `VERIFY_JOBS` sets the worker count; the default is the CPU count (4 on GitHub's Linux runners).
- With one job, or where `fork` is unavailable, it runs the original serial loop.

`certificate.json` changes only in the pinned SHA-256 of `verify.py`, which the verifier hashes into its own certificate:

```
-    "research/recycled-bit-integration/verify.py": "25a31677…e218",
+    "research/recycled-bit-integration/verify.py": "a5508f42…a0b9",
```

`docs/research/community-round7-validation.json` records the old certificate hash as a historical validation record. No script reads it, so it is left as written.

## Measured locally (Python 3.11, 4 workers)

| | `verify.py --all` |
|---|---:|
| before (serial) | 12 min 23 s |
| after | **5 min 59 s** |

The `--all --write` run passed every check and reproduced the certificate apart from the hash line. `test_recycled_bit_integration.py` passes (3 tests). On CI this should bring the group down to about 6 minutes, making the `research` group and `formal (historical)` (about 10–11 minutes each) the new critical path, for an estimated ~17 → ~11 minutes wall time.

I also tried precomputing each distinct frame basis once across workers instead. It was slower (7 min 14 s), because the basis keys depend on each other and don't split evenly, so the simpler chunking is used.

Possible follow-ups, for the maintainers to decide: caching the project's Lean build when `formal/lean` is unchanged (567 s of the 671 s `formal (historical)` job), and running independent `verify-research` targets in parallel after checking they don't write the same files.

Prepared by Joel Pulikkan with Anthropic Claude assistance.
